diagnosis:
Why hero U now feels weaker than the approved page below it:

1) It is the only section with no instrument. Every section below proves its claim with one exact 1px drawing: the iso block with its red datum, the three strata with the red slab, six folio sheets crossing a handover datum, the phase gantt, the ten-tick ruler. The hero's whole content is type laid over a picture. That is the most common hero on the web: on Mobbin, Harvey ('Practice Made Perfect'), Square, Jasper, komoot and Shopify all use the same full-bleed people film with a left headline (see refs/hero-r6-10.webp). Its only drafting traces are two + marks on the nav hairline.

2) The video is wallpaper, not a subject. It fills everything, so it frames nothing. It runs at 8px blur and .20 frost, under a scrim that holds the left quarter at 78–90% graphite and the floor at 82%. What survives is a warm brown smear in the upper right. Nothing tells the eye 'this is footage': no edge, no cut, no focus change, no time. In a still it reads as a dim stock photo. Its motion is a 32s drift plus one 1.6s pull-back, both too slow to notice.

3) It is the only soft surface on a hard-edged page. Everything below is flat graphite or paper, built from hairlines, plates and registration marks. The hero alone is gradient scrim plus frost. The same type on a softer material reads as a different, more 'agency' brand.

4) The subject says nothing about the work. People in a room is the default B2B image, and nothing in the frame shows narrative, channel or intelligence systems being run. Defense and infrastructure sites (Anduril, Palantir, Helsing) show the thing operating: soft footage, framed as evidence, with crisp drawn UI over it.

5) The act ends in mud. The lower 40% (note, lede and doors) floats as small grey type over the lowest-contrast part of the picture, and the only red is the button. Round 4 rightly removed the band (caption, ruler, timecode, Pause), because those were captions rather than instruments. Once it went, nothing was left to make the film read as footage.

The fix is not more overlay. The video needs a job (evidence, optics, cinema or terrain) and one drawn device that gives it edges and meaning. The four concepts below each give it one.

concepts.name: The Operating Feed
concepts.idea: The room stops being wallpaper and becomes evidence. The full-bleed film is gone and the hero sits on flat graphite, like every section below. Its one artifact is a framed live feed: the engagement room in three hard-cut takes, one per system Kelwin runs. Under the frame, a calibrated chapter rail names each take: 01 Narrative Systems, 02 GTM Infrastructure, 03 GTM Intelligence. It works like the 'feed' monitor in a defense ops room, except what is being monitored is the system being installed. The video is the subject of an instrument. Everything is drawn in the page's own grammar: hairline frame, corner registration marks, a MEASURE ruler as the scrub bar, and the nav's capability glyphs as chapter marks.
concepts.video: MOCKUP: one .km-film inside the frame (plate + walker + frost + grain) using img/film-room.webp at --film-blur 8px (the contract floor), frost .12 and grain .5. JS re-frames the plate into three takes and cuts hard between them. Take 01 is a close crop on the standing colleague at the wall (the narrative workshop). Take 02 is the seated figure at the screen (the infrastructure build). Take 03 is the wide room with the man from behind (the intelligence review). A thin top scrim inside .km-film makes room for the one mono line. PRODUCTION: commissioned 4K/24fps footage from a real client working session, shot through reeded/fluted glass. The frost is optical, so identities are never readable but gestures are. Three 8s takes: hands mapping a narrative on a wall; a screen of routing and sequence logic; a weekly signal review around a table. Graded warm-graphite and delivered as one 24s loop (H.265 MP4 + VP9 WebM, about 4 MB), muted, playsinline, with take 01 as poster. Chapter seeks are just currentTime jumps to 0, 8 and 16s.
concepts.layout: Stage 1440×960 on flat --bg. No film outside the frame. Nav (0–96) exactly as in U: lockup, centred tracked caps, outlined AUDIT REQUEST ↗, margin-to-margin hairline, + marks at (64,96) and (1376,96). The head sits top-left. The ■ GTM systems partner label is at y 148. The statement is two lines at 116px from y 184 to 407: 'Revenue is an' spans cols 1–7 (ends x 819) and 'architectural problem.' spans cols 1–11. The 48×2 red rule sits at y 447. The FEED is in cols 1–7 (x 64–819), y 486–826: 755×340, about 2.2:1. It has a 1px --line frame and four corner + marks (6 marks in total, at quota). Inside the frame, top-left, one mono line (11px, .10em, --fg-2, ≤ 40 characters): 'WORKING SESSION · 01/03 · 00:00:12'. Under the frame, the CHAPTER RAIL: a 1px baseline ruler at y 838 with 24 minor ticks (one per second of the loop), major ticks at 0/8/16s and a 1px --fg playhead. Chapter labels sit at y 852–870 in three equal thirds (x 64 / 316 / 568), each a mono index plus a Mona 14px name. The active chapter is --fg and its nav glyph (CONTOUR / TRACE / ORBIT, 36×24) is drawn after the name; the inactive ones are --fg-3. RIGHT BAY, cols 8–12 (x 843–1376): the ■ A fixed-scope diagnostic note is top-aligned with the frame (y 486). The 20px lede (3 lines) sits at y about 704–789. The doors (cut-corner red 'Request a System Audit' → /audit, underlined 'Talk to the team →' → /contact) sit at y 814–870, justified across the bay as in U, with their bottom on the chapter-rail baseline. That keeps them above a 1440×900 fold. Reading path: statement (top-left) → feed (bottom-left) → action (bottom-right). Red appears only on the label squares, the rule and the primary. FLAG: the statement is anchored at the top rather than 'almost vertically centred', and the audit note moves from bottom-left to the head of the right bay, because the feed takes that corner.
concepts.motion: Entrance (≤ 1.6s): the nav hairline draws and its marks register; the label and the two statement lines rise from their masks (kit choreography); the rule draws. The frame then plots in drafting order: dashed construction lines run along its top and left edges at 600–900ms, the 1px outline closes, and the four corner marks register. The picture fades up inside on take 01 (600ms). The chapter ruler calibrates left to right (20ms stagger), chapter 01 latches, and its CONTOUR glyph draws (600ms). Orchestrated moment: at 2.4s a hard cut to take 02. The playhead jumps to the second major tick, 02 latches and the TRACE glyph draws. The demo cuts to 03 (ORBIT) at 4.0s. Ambient: on the live site the takes cut every 8s on a 24s loop, the playhead travels linearly, and the frost grain flickers. This is the only loop. Interaction: clicking or tapping a chapter seeks the film to that take, and auto-cycling stops for good after the first interaction, which is the founder's 'let them skim' rule from the System section. Hovering a chapter turns it --fg. Reduced motion: a poster frame of take 01, chapter 01 active, no cuts and no playhead travel.
concepts.why_not_agency: Agencies run a showreel behind the headline as mood. T contains the film and gives it instrument furniture that carries information: which take, how far in, and which system is on screen. It reads as an operations console showing the work being done, not a brand film. It also sits on the same flat graphite, hairline frame and calibrated ruler as every plate below, so the hero becomes the page's first instrument rather than its only photograph. Sunday's research-video card makes the same move: footage presented as evidence, not atmosphere.

refs.takeaway: The film is a contained card on black with one quiet label ('Research Video 2025'), so it reads as R&D evidence, not atmosphere. Kelwin: the card becomes a hairline-framed feed with registration marks and a mono session line.

Framed footage on a dark page with a strip of takes under it, so you know there is more than one shot. Kelwin: the strip becomes three clickable chapters, keyed to the three systems, on a calibrated MEASURE ruler.
A framed film with one subtitle line inside the frame that gives the footage a voice. Kelwin: one mono line (session · take · time), never a sentence, at the 11px floor.

concepts.name: The Scope
concepts.idea: Keep the founder's full-bleed frosted room exactly as in U. Add the one device that turns it into a subject: a fixed rectangular SCOPE of clear glass, set on the grid in the open upper-right of the room. Outside the scope the footage stays frosted, which is fragmented growth as the market sees it. Inside, the same footage is pin-registered and in focus. The scope is the System Audit drawn as an optical instrument. It is a fixed scope (the pane never moves), its bottom edge is calibrated into ten equal day cells (ten working days), and the primary button sits directly beneath it on the same column line. When a silhouette walks through the pane it sharpens, then frosts again as it leaves. The video now carries the thesis: we make the architecture visible.
concepts.video: MOCKUP: U's film unchanged: img/film-room.webp, blur 8px, frost .20, bright 1.26, grain .5, the same height-fit plate and the same scrim. A second .km-film__plate layer sits inside the same .km-film, clipped to the pane with clip-path: inset(...). It runs at --film-blur 0–1.5px, frost 0, brightness about +8% and no scrim, and shares the drift keyframes and walker so both layers stay registered pixel for pixel. PRODUCTION: one 4K/24fps, 30s seamless loop of the working session (the same commission as today's film), shot with shallow depth of field and faces turned away, so nothing is identifiable even where it is sharp. Render it with ONE <video> drawn sharp full-bleed. The frost is a sibling glass layer inside .km-film (backdrop-filter: blur(10px) plus the frost tint and grain) whose clip-path has an even-odd hole the shape of the pane. That gives one decode, perfect registration and a cheap focus pull (animate the hole's blur and tint). FLAG: the 8–12px frost rule is kept for the room; only the inside of the scope is sharp, by design.
concepts.layout: Stage 1440×960, U's layout untouched. Nav over the film. The ■ label is at y 284. The two-line 116px statement is held at about 45%: 'Revenue is an' spans cols 1–7 (ends x 819) and 'architectural problem.' spans cols 1–11. The red rule sits 40px under it. The lede and the justified doors are bottom-right in cols 8–12 (y about 650–824, above the fold). The audit note is bottom-left in cols 1–4, with its last baseline on the primary's bottom edge. THE SCOPE: cols 8–12 (x 843–1376, 533 wide), y 128–332 (204 tall, about 2.6:1). That is the open upper-right where U already 'shows the room'. It stays clear of line 1 (a 24px gutter and a different row) and ends about 120px above line 2's cap height. It has a 1px --fg outline and four corner + marks (6 marks in total with the nav pair). Its bottom edge is a ten-cell day ruler: 4px minor ticks rise inside the frame, with 8px majors at day 01 and day 10. One mono label (11px, .10em, --fg-2) is right-aligned under its right end at y about 350: '10 WORKING DAYS'. There is no other text, crosshair or reticle, and the pane never tracks anyone. The col-8 line becomes the hero's spine: the scope's left edge, the lede and the primary button all stand on it. Red appears on the label squares, the rule and the primary only.
concepts.motion: Entrance: the film fades up fully frosted (1.2s) while the nav hairline draws and the statement lands with U's choreography. U's close→wide pull-back is retired; this move replaces it. Construction (0.9–1.6s): dashed construction lines extend along the pane's top and left edges, the 1px outline closes, the four corner marks register, and the ten day ticks calibrate left to right (40ms stagger). The label fades in. Orchestrated moment (about 1.8–3.4s): a focus pull. Inside the pane the frost clears (blur 8→0, frost .20→0, 1.6s ease-inout) and the room resolves through the scope while everything around it stays frosted. Ambient: the 32s drift and the walker continue. Each silhouette sharpens as it crosses the pane and frosts as it leaves. That is the only loop. Interaction (live, optional): hovering 'Request a System Audit' steps a 1px --fg fill across the ten day cells (30ms stagger) and back on leave, so the visitor sees the scope they are booking. Reduced motion: final state, with the pane clear, the film still on the wide framing and no drift.
concepts.why_not_agency: An agency blurs a lifestyle video for mood. V makes the blur mean something: the market is frosted, and the fixed-scope diagnostic is the one place it is clear. The device is a precise optical instrument (a hard 1px gate, registration marks, a calibrated ruler, a real focus pull), the kind of artifact a Zeiss or Palantir design team would draw. It ties the footage to the conversion, because the scope is the audit and the button sits under it. And it keeps the founder's own room, so this is the continuity option.

refs.takeaway: A frame inside a frame turns a flat plate into an optical device that pulls the eye through to the moving image. Kelwin: a flat 1px scope over the frosted film, with clarity inside it and no perspective tunnel.

A small, sharper inset registered inside a hazy full-bleed defense film, so the inset is the thing being looked at. Kelwin: not a tracking box but a fixed pane on the 12-column grid, which follows the founder's 'nothing tracking the people' rule.

A calibration drawn around the film turns 'watch' into a measured instrument. Kelwin: a straight ten-day ruler on the pane's edge (dial bezels and reticles are banned), which echoes the final CTA's ten ticks.

concepts.name: The Wide Frame
concepts.idea: Treat the footage as cinema, not backdrop. The hero becomes a cinema frame. A single full-width band in Ultra Panavision 70 proportions (2.76:1) holds the film. Flat graphite bars above and below it carry the interface: the nav on top, the lede, doors and audit note below, all crisp on flat colour. The statement sits inside the band like a title card. The page's own drafting grammar opens it: the nav hairline draws, splits in two, and the lower line descends to open the film between them. A line becomes a picture. There are no captions, timecodes or controls; the hard frame is the device.
concepts.video: MOCKUP: img/film-room.webp in a .km-film confined to the band (absolute container 1440×522, overflow hidden). The plate is scaled so the three silhouettes (the man from behind, the standing colleague, the seated one) sit across the band at head height. Settings: blur 8px, frost .16, bright 1.2, grain .5, the walker on, and a left-only scrim inside .km-film behind the statement. A slow lateral pan replaces the zoom drift (translateX ±3% over 40s, alternate). PRODUCTION: commissioned anamorphic 4K footage (2.39:1 native, extracted to 2.76:1). One continuous 40s slow lateral dolly along a glass-walled working session at night, shot through frosted glass so the frost is optical. Graded graphite with warm practicals, a ping-pong or seamless loop, muted, playsinline, with the poster on the three-figure frame.
concepts.layout: Stage 1440×960. Nav (0–96) sits on flat --bg, unchanged from U. THE BAND: full-bleed, x 0–1440 × y 96–618 (522 tall = 2.76:1). Its top edge is the nav hairline itself. A second margin-to-margin hairline marks its bottom edge at y 618. + marks sit where the band edges cross the margins: (64,96), (1376,96), (64,618) and (1376,618), 4 in total. INSIDE THE BAND, on film: the ■ GTM systems partner label at y 196; the two-line 116px statement at y 232–455 ('Revenue is an' in cols 1–7, 'architectural problem.' in cols 1–11), optically centred in the band at about 37% of the stage; the 48×2 red rule at y 495. THE BOTTOM BAR (y 618–960) is flat --bg with no scrim. The 20px lede sits in cols 8–12 at y 658–748. The justified doors sit in cols 8–12 at y 776–832, above the 1440×900 fold. The audit note sits in cols 1–4, its last baseline on the primary's bottom edge (832), exactly U's relationship. The founder's diagonal (statement mid-left → action bottom-right, note bottom-left) is kept intact, but the action now sits on hard flat colour. Red appears on the label squares, the rule and the primary. FLAG (brand family): Plurel's move is a full-width film band BENEATH the headline. Here the headline sits INSIDE the band, the band is the frame of the whole hero, and its edges are Kelwin hairlines with registration marks. Keep it that way.
concepts.motion: Entrance: the nav hairline draws left to right (0–1.0s), as every section's hairline does. At 0.9s it splits: a second hairline peels away and descends from y 96 to y 618 (1.2s ease-inout). The film is revealed between the two lines (the band's clip-path follows the descending line), so a line opens into a film. The four + marks register as the line lands. The label and statement rise inside the opening band (kit choreography, --ac-d0 about 900ms) and the red rule draws. The lede, doors and note then fade up on the flat bar (+700ms). Ambient: one slow lateral dolly, the walker crossing, and grain; this is the only loop. On the live site the film plays muted and loops, the band never pins, and the page continues with reveal-on-scroll only. Reduced motion: the band open on a still frame, with no pan.
concepts.why_not_agency: An agency reel fills the screen and fights the type with gradients. W gives the footage the dignity of a real cinema format: a hard-edged 2.76:1 frame with flat bars and no scrim on the interface, like the title card of a defense brand film. The opening is built from the page's own hairline grammar rather than a video-player effect. The restraint (no furniture at all) is the luxury signal, and the crisp flat bottom bar fixes U's 'action floating in mud'.

refs.takeaway: A two-tone headline over dark, letterboxed footage of people. The hard crop is what makes it read as cinema rather than wallpaper. Kelwin: a full-width 2.76:1 band with the statement set inside it as a title card.
Footage cut by a hard flat seam, so the film has edges and the flat colour does the structural work. Kelwin: flat graphite bars above and below the band, and a seam that opens from the nav hairline.

The category default today's hero sits too close to: a full-bleed dark film of people at work under a left headline. W keeps the people but gives them a cinema frame and moves the action onto flat colour.

concepts.name: The Survey
concepts.idea: Range option, with no people. The video is the market seen from directly above: a slow nadir survey of a city grid at night, whose blocks, streets and moving lights read as territory and signal at scale. Over it, Kelwin's own instrument is registered to the streets: a crisp 1px TRACE route that enters as dashed raw signal from the left edge and turns solid at the col-8 line. It latches three nodes on three blocks (01 Narrative Systems · 02 GTM Infrastructure · 03 GTM Intelligence) and drops toward the doors in one open chevron. One packet laps the route at constant speed while the footage's own traffic moves every which way. That pairing is fragmented growth against repeatable pipeline, the lede made visible. Footage is soft and the drawing is crisp, which is the defense-software look in Kelwin's vocabulary. The video is essential: the route only exists on its territory.
concepts.video: MOCKUP (procedural, no new footage): a <canvas> plate inside .km-film, replacing .km-film__plate, renders an orthographic top-down night grid. It uses a seeded PRNG (mulberry32): blocks are flat fills read from tokens (--panel / --panel-2, ±4% luminance), streets are --bg, and a few avenues are one step lighter. Sparse 2px lights in sand/fog tones at 40–60% alpha travel along street centrelines at 6–14px/s. A large soft cloud-shadow drifts across in 40s (alpha .10, canvas compositing only, no CSS gradients). The whole plate pans 2% over 40s as a pure translate, and the canvas is drawn at devicePixelRatio. It sits under the standard frost and grain at --film-blur 8px and frost .22, which reads as aerial footage through haze. PRODUCTION: licensed 4K nadir (straight-down) drone or helicopter footage of a dense orthogonal city grid at night, unidentifiable after grading. 40s, a pure lateral pan with no rotation or zoom, graded graphite with warm sand lights and no neon. Alternatively, a rendered orthographic flyover of a procedural grid with instanced traffic (Blender/Houdini), exported as a seamless 30s loop together with per-frame node positions. The SVG route either rides the same CSS translate as the video or reads those offsets, so it stays pinned to its streets.
concepts.layout: Stage 1440×960, with U's type positions so the founder's diagonal holds. Nav over the film. The ■ label is at y 284. The two-line 116px statement sits at about 45% (line 1 in cols 1–7, line 2 in cols 1–11) with the red rule below it. The lede and justified doors are in cols 8–12 (y about 650–824). The audit note is in cols 1–4 bottom-left. A left scrim inside .km-film works as in U. THE ROUTE (SVG, 1px --fg, 90° turns only, ≤ 6 nodes) runs in the free upper zone and down the right margin. A dashed lead-in (--fg-3) enters from x 0 along an avenue at y 200 (84px above the label) across cols 1–7. It turns solid at node 01 (843, 200) on the col-8 line, which is the same spine as the lede and the primary. It runs right to node 02 at col 10 (1066, 200), continues to x 1289 (col 12), and turns down a street to node 03 (1289, 392). It then continues down x 1289, clearing line 2's end at x 1238, and stops at y 612 in one open chevron above the lede. The nodes are 7px squares, outlined and then filled when latched. There are three callouts above or left of their nodes: a mono code box plus a Mona 14px name, 9 words in all, each linking to /capabilities. One 6px --fg packet runs on the solid route. There is no red in the drawing; red stays on the label squares, the rule and the primary. FLAG: this drops the people-at-work film, the founder's original DNA, deliberately, to show the most high-tech end of the range.
concepts.motion: Entrance: the film fades up (1.2s) and the statement lands with the kit choreography. From 0.9s the route draws in reading order, segment by segment (pathLength 1, 1.4s ease-inout in total). The dashed lead-in comes first, then the solid route; each node latches as the line reaches it (outline → filled, 200ms), its callout fades in, and the chevron seats last (about 2.6s). Ambient: one 6px packet laps the solid route at constant speed (≥ 8s per lap, linear). This is the only drawn loop, alongside the footage's own pan and traffic. On the live site the route is pinned to the footage, so it never slides off its streets. Hovering a callout brightens its segment to --fg and dims the others to --fg-3. Reduced motion: the route drawn, nodes latched, no packet, a still frame.
concepts.why_not_agency: No lifestyle footage and no mood. Z speaks the visual language of defense and infrastructure software (a nadir survey of territory with a crisp routed overlay) but draws it entirely in Kelwin's own 1px TRACE primitive, in flat tokens, with no glow, no perspective horizon and no Tron floor. The footage is the market and the drawing is the system Kelwin installs, so the video is the ground the instrument reads, not décor behind a headline.

refs.takeaway: A slow aerial as an enterprise hero: terrain reads as scale and seriousness, not lifestyle. Kelwin: straight-down orthographic, graded graphite, no horizon, and the type on U's grid.

Footage that is itself data (light columns) behind a left headline, so the video reads as infrastructure. Kelwin: the data is the city's own traffic, and Kelwin's single routed path is drawn crisply on top of it.

A crisp instrument sitting on soft aerial footage under 'complexity into clarity'. The contrast of soft ground and sharp tool is the message. Kelwin: the tool is a 1px TRACE route registered to the streets, not a product screenshot.
